newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan watchdog says big share volumes acceptable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan watchdog says big share volumes acceptable.

text.p: Taiwan's watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission has said heavy stock trading volume is acceptable as long as the market remains orderly, commission officials said on Wednesday.
Commission chairman Lu Tung-ying said in an internal meeting late on Tuesday that there was nothing to be afraid of when turnover was heavy, an aide told Reuters by telephone.
"As long as the market is in order and healthy -- that is, with timely transactions, no irregularities and reasonable investment -- large trade turnover is acceptable," the aide quoted Lu as saying.
Lu said large turnover meant active investment, which would enable listed companies to raise more funds and, in turn, boost domestic investment and help develop the economy.
Turnover in the main Taiwan Stock Exchange surged to its highest levels in three years late in February, hitting T$179.27 billion (US$6.5 billion) on February 26.

Lu's comments, reported by some morning newspapers, helped spur market momentum on Wednesday with the stock index slicing through resistance at 8,000 after several days of anxiety over central bank monetary policy.

Analysts said the statement countered central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung's warning on Saturday that individual investors should exercise caution in a big rally that had added more than 1,000 points to the index in 1997.
"Investors are feeling freer from worries now," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
The central bank official's caution had sent the index tumbling 1.29 percent on Monday, although the index gained most of that back on Tuesday.
